title: Bound on every minimal component dimension
statement: Let k be a field and S a commutative finite type k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let p be a prime ideal and d,r natural numbers with dim(S_p)=d [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and trdeg_k(kappa(p))=r [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Every minimal prime q of S contained in p satisfies dim(S/q) <= d+r.

proof.text: put A = S/q and let P be the image of p in A. Ideal correspondence identifies primes of A with primes of S containing q. The residue field of P is canonically the residue field of p; it is the fraction field of A/P = S/p. Thus the finite type domain dimension/transcendence-degree theorem gives `dim(S/p) = r`. The maximal-chain theorem for that domain supplies a saturated chain from p to a maximal ideal of S of length r. Since hd bounds every chain below p by d, choose a longest chain from q to p, of length s <= d. Such a chain exists: q <= p, and the set of possible natural lengths is nonempty and bounded by d. It is saturated, and its first member is q. Append the chosen chain above p, counting p only once. In the domain A, the resulting chain starts at zero, ends at a maximal ideal, and is saturated, hence is a maximal chain. The finite type domain maximal-chain theorem says its length s+r is dim(A). Therefore dim(S/q) = s+r <= d+r.
